But I think the Defence also should be aware that these views, in part, serves their own interests, especially as regards the intent, the underlying intent which will be one crucial point in our case. And therefore, it's always helpful to hear these individual views because one of the purposes, and one of the reasons, why we are mandated to exercise our work here is to find the roots, the reasons, the basics of what happened there and how we can overcome these difficulties in order to have people living peacefully together once again in the area of Former Yugoslavia. And therefore, under this mandate, opposed to ordinary courts, it's necessary to put these questions. I see Mr. Koumjian arriving. And maybe --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do need a break, though, because we haven't been able to -- it's quite a long tape. It's not the excerpt tape. It's the full tape. So we'll have to ask Your Honours for a break to set this up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be possible to do it within five minutes that we can conclude the testimony, say, until 10 minutes past 1.00?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, may I ask, then, I know it's unusual, but when I said to Your Honour yesterday that I didn't think the other case would require my attention, it is going to require my attention and will from about 12.00. Would Your Honour forgive me and allow Mr. Koumjian just to deal with the last part of this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt. I think the remaining part is to view the video and to hear the comments by the witness on this video. So we have a break now for about five minutes. Please, all standby and let us know when we can start. --- Break taken at 12.44 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. May we now see the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have two very, very short clips. The first one is from the ERN number V0000285. And, Doctor, watch this. And please correct me if I am wrong if this is not the main street of Kozarac, but the main road passing along Kozarac between Prijedor and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Omarska.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think that this was taken from the road, although now I cannot see any specific landmarks. So I'm not sure. But I think that it was taken from the road, the Kozarac/Banja Luka Road looking in the direction of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it possible to dim the lights a bit in the courtroom? Sorry, I notice the screen was much easier to read in the video booth than it is out here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm afraid it will be extremely difficult because we have the cameras, and they need the light for the cameras.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I see. If we could proceed and play the video. And, Doctor, you can indicate at any time if you'd like to stop and comment upon anything that you recognise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think that's the end of the clip of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Doctor, did you recognise any of the buildings or the section of the road that was depicted on the video that was just played?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any particular landmarks, so I'm not able to tell you whether that exactly is the spot. We were moving from Kozarac towards Prijedor, and that was the area that I saw during the shelling when we were captured. As for the other part that I didn't see, I'm unable to compare the situation as it was before with the one that was after. I saw a video footage when the road leading into Kozarac could be seen. It was filmed from the road going towards Kozarac. I remember that particular one, but here I cannot tell you with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just ask you a few questions about the road that passed between Prijedor and Omarska alongside Kozarac. To get to Kozarac itself is a short distance from that main road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The south side of Kozarac town is situated alongside the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. So if you were passing --

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the building that we saw when we stopped the film is the cafe located at the junction to the right side of the approach road to Kozarac. But because I was not a hundred per cent sure, I didn't want to make that comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would that video that you saw be consistent with the area that you knew to be a view from the main road looking north towards Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were being escorted from Kozarac -- I mean, at one point, we turned left towards Prijedor. We turned right towards Prijedor, and we left -- to the left was the road leading to Banja Luka. I think the cafe that we saw was located at the corner, at the junction, of that road. But what happened afterwards further down on the road towards Banja Luka, I don't know. I didn't pay any attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: After your release from the Trnopolje camp, did you ever visit Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You've never been back to Kozarac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I have one more short clip to ask you to view. And that would be -- I have the ERN number, V0002843. If that tape could be played, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We could play the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we play the tape with the sound. It might be -- it might give some explanation of what we're seeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just got it a moment ago.

utterances.text: Perhaps we could back up since the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The image was not on my screen a moment ago, but I can see it now. To the right, you see a cross, and to the left, a Serbian flag. utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps we could back up the tape because the witness did not have it on his screen. Start it over again with the sound, please. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop, please. "The Narrator: ...today there are no Muslims there, none. And none of their X-marked homes is intact. Other homes in Kozarac have been marked to survive --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think the witness had a comment back at the first house if we could back up, he'll indicate where to stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this house is located on the approach road to Kozarac, to the right side of the road. utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And, Doctor, when you talk about the house you just mentioned, you're not talking about the house that's on the screen in front of you with the sign saying --

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: This is the house that you were speaking of?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We can proceed with the video, just to complete it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Doctor, do you know, the clip that you're speaking of showing the main street, was that where the -- there's a video of that clip being shown to some women who were residents of Kozarac? And one of them makes a remark that "this was the most beautiful house"?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but I think that I have the footage you're talking about at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the OTP, the two videos we saw today, they are tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: They are, Your Honour. The only issue is, although we don't mind tendering the entire tape, we didn't play the entire tape. Would Your Honour like us to have copies made of those clips that were shown?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, because no doubt we have to come back to these points. It's relevant to find out what's the meaning of this cross marking and the marking with the flag. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. This concludes the testimony, and I have to re-emphasise the gratitude of the parties and the Bench that you were prepared to come here and to give the witness on these incidents - we have to be neutral naming these "incidents" - evidently opening once again wounds with you. And thereby, we know how difficult it is for you to give these statements. But you should be aware that your testimony has, once again, assisted us one step further to coming closer to the truth. And we are extremely grateful for this. Thank you once again. The trial stays adjourned until 2.50, 10 minutes to 3.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.16 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. As discussed already yesterday in a 65 ter (i) meeting, also for the purposes of our transcript, the parties have to be informed that Judge Fassi Fihri will not be in The Hague before, seen from an optimistic point of view, the middle of next week, and in all likelihood not earlier than the Monday starting the week after next week. So therefore, we discussed already yesterday how to proceed. And as Rule 15 bis does not allow for proceeding with only two Judges for a period of time longer than three days, this period of time elapses today. On the other hand, it's necessary to have heard these witnesses who are prepared to testify in this case in the near future without asking them to come a second time to The Hague. And first of all, we have to take care that it's mandatory under the statute to proceed as fast as possible. So therefore, the idea is that the witnesses planned now for the near future, until the end of the Prosecutor's case, should be heard under Rule 71 of the rules. This means that it's the most appropriate way to hear these witnesses. It provides for the possibility that both parties put questions to the witness, that we have a real examination, cross-examination, and if the then present accused so wants, he also may address the presiding officer under Rule 71. And in addition, it means that the results of this examination under Rule 71 have to be included in the hearing once more under Rule 71(E) of the rules, and this gives additional leeway for both parties to comment on the outcome of these hearings. No doubt, on the other hand, it means that the hearings take place in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri. Therefore, as discussed yesterday, we regard it as necessary that we have the consent by the parties that we proceed this way and that the accused, Dr. Stakic himself, consents to this proceeding in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri. This would be so Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that there is no doubt about the scope of application, this would cover the following witnesses: Mr. Edward Vulliamy, to be expected on Monday and Tuesday; Madam Ewa Tabeau and Mr. Nicolas Sebire, this would be not a continuation of the earlier hearing, but it would be a separate hearing under Rule 71. It would be true also for Dr. Corin and for Dr. Ewan Brown. And finally, for Mr. Dusan Baltic. May I ask the parties whether they consent to this envisaged proceeding? First, the OTP, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had the opportunity to speak with Dr. Stakic, and you have his full consent to proceed this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask Dr. Stakic in person, do you agree with these proceedings under Rule 71 in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I fully agree to proceed as you have just advised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. As to the fact that we discussed this issue already yesterday, I have to read out the following decision unanimously found by the two Judges present in this case. It's an order for deposition evidence to be taken pursuant to Rule 71 of 11 September, 2002. The written version may be corrected, please. It reads: "This Trial Chamber of the International Tribunal for the Prosecution of Persons Responsible for Serious Violations of International Humanitarian Law Committed in the Territory of the Former Yugoslavia since 1991, "Noting that one of the Judges of this Trial Chamber, namely Judge Fassi Fihri, is temporarily unavailable to sit in court due to ongoing illness, "Noting that on 6 September, 2002, the two present Judges of this Trial Chamber ordered, pursuant to Rule 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, that the hearing of this case continue in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri for the maximum period of three days permitted under the Rules, "Noting further that as of the end of today, 11 September, 2002, the three-day period will have expired; noting that Rule 71 of the Rules set out a procedure permitting evidence for use at trial to be taken by way of deposition, "Noting that pursuant to Rule 71(A) of the Rules, the Trial Chamber, where it is in the interests of justice to do so, may order, either proprio motu or at the request of a party, that deposition evidence be taken before a duly appointed Presiding Officer, "Noting the agreement of the parties in this case to the use of this procedure for direct and cross-examination of the following witnesses, subject to any decisions on objections and matters of admissibility being reserved to the Trial Chamber: Mr. Dusan Baltic, Dr. Ewan Brown, Dr. Andrew Corin, Mr. Nicolas Sebire, Madam Ewa Tabeau, Mr. Edward Vulliamy, "Noting in particular that the accused, Dr. Milomir Stakic, has consented to the use of this procedure, "Noting further that the accused has agreed that Judge Vassylenko may be present in the courtroom during the deposition proceedings" -- sorry, I forgot to ask you this question, Dr. Stakic: Do you agree that Judge Vassylenko may be present in the courtroom during the proceedings under Rule 71?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I fully agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to take this opportunity to ask you to please forward my regards and best wishes concerning his health to the ailing Judge Fassi Fihri.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will do so. You may be seated. I repeat the last paragraph: "Noting further that the accused has agreed that Judge Vassylenko may be present in the courtroom during the deposition proceedings, "Considering that the unavailability of one of the members of the Trial Chamber must not prejudice the right of the accused to be tried without undue delay as provided in Article 21, paragraph 4(c) of the statute of the International Tribunal, "Considering the guidance on the interpretation of Rule 71(A) by the Appeals Chamber of the International Tribunal in its decision of 15 July, 1999, in Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic and others, "Considering that the accused has explicitly consented to take depositions under Rule 71 of the Rules in the case in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri, "For the foregoing reasons and with the consent of the parties and the accused, "Pursuant to Article 21 of the statute and Rules 15 bis, 54, and 71 of the rules, orders proprio motu, that the evidence of the aforementioned witnesses, namely, Mr. Baltic, Dr. Brown, Dr. Corin, Mr. Sebire, Madam Tabeau, and Mr. Vulliamy may, be taken pursuant to Rule 71 of the rules, such procedure to cease immediately upon the return of Judge Fassi Fihri to active duty, "Appoints as Presiding Officer for that purpose Judge Wolfgang Schomburg, and further orders that the deposition procedure shall be as follows: "First, the depositions to be taken in a courtroom at the seat of the International Tribunal during the normal court sessions as previously scheduled; second, Judge Vassylenko may be present in the courtroom during the deposition proceedings; third, all participants to be robed as usual; fourth, the hearings to be public subject to any protective measures that may be ordered in relation to particular witnesses; fifth, the record to be transmitted to the Trial Chamber comprising three Judges, pursuant to Rule 71(E) of the Rules. "Done in English and French, the English text being authoritative, followed by a signature of the Judge." Any observations to this procedure?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just one extremely technical observation. I think that Your Honour said that it would be a new hearing of witnesses Sebire and Tabeau, I think at least as far as Mr. Sebire when we ended, Mr. Ostojic said that he had two more questions, although when I spoke to him the other day on the phone, he said he had completed his cross-examination. But technically I think the Defence did not complete the cross-examination while Judge Fassi Fihri was here. So I would ask that they indicate that they do not wish to have any further questions in front of the three Judges that are -- that they can complete their questioning in the deposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Respectfully, we disagree. We discussed this because we expect a new document by this witness, and no doubt, this has to be introduced, and the Defence has the right to cross-examine the author of this new document, and it's also the right of the Judges to have additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I understand that, but technically they didn't finish the cross-examination in front of the three Judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm aware of this, but on the occasion of taking this deposition, it will be the possibility, if any, to put questions to Mr. Sebire during taking this deposition under Rule 71. I see a nodding by the Defence. I think there is no additional problem with this. Then I have numerous additional points on the agenda. And before starting, may I ask the Prosecution if there should be any additional document to be provided today, it should be done during the next 90 minutes. If there should be any motion, please do it orally. This goes to both parties. As to the fact that we can't do this during the application of Rule 71 because this is limited to hear the witnesses only. The intention is to discuss how to proceed in the framework of a Status Conference, and a Status Conference -- the next Status Conference in this case is hereby scheduled for Tuesday immediately following the taking of a deposition with respect to the witness of Monday and Tuesday. And if necessary, to proceed with this Status Conference by Wednesday morning. And this will be then the appropriate place to discuss issues as already announced by the Prosecution whether or not it is helpful to have deliberations. I'll come back to this later. Next point: I received a letter by attorney at law Vojislav Dimitrijevic, counsel of Mr. Mrdja, resulting in the sentence that counsel decided to advise Mr. Mrdja not to testify in this moment voluntarily in the case of Mr. Stakic because it can hurt his own Defence. In the conversation with client, he fully accepted my advice. May I ask the usher to distribute copies of this letter to the parties and to the registry. This will be, then, Document J12. It was not without surprise that we received a motion by the Prosecution for Rule 94, judicial notice. Are there any additional comments on this motion by the representative of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to explain, if Your Honour -- apparently Your Honour was surprised, this is part of the indictment for which no witnesses were presented. I don't know if it would be proper for me to tell you the reasons why no witnesses were presented because I think that would probably be outside the evidence. But we believe it's a litigated issue in the Tadic decision, and since we are unable to present evidence in this case on it, we believe it has been fully litigated as far as the fact that that massacre took place, or those killings took place, who the perpetrators were, and findings were made as to the motivation for the killings. We think that it's appropriate under Rule 94 to take judicial notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask for observations by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This was subject to lengthy discussions before the beginning of this trial. And already at that time, we objected to any facts established in the Tadic case because Mr. Tadic defended himself by alibi, and he didn't oppose any fact. So we think that in that procedure, it wasn't established that something has been done or not because the other side, the Defence, didn't object on any factual ground of the indictment. And we think today, as we thought at that time, that the Prosecution has to establish all factual grounds for the indictment during the Court proceedings in this case. So we think that this motion should be rejected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I recall the former objections by the Defence. And may I first ask the Prosecution why witnesses for these alleged facts were not presented? And secondly, whether it would not be mandatory for reasons of judicial economy to drop - I mentioned this earlier - to drop those parts in the indictment where no evidence has been found because for whatever reasons, no evidence was available. We are aware of the problems of both problems to bring witnesses to The Hague. But nevertheless, it seems for me mandatory to take into account the costs of the proceedings and to take into account the right of the accused, which no doubt would be limited by taking judicial notice, whether or not it would be appropriate to drop these parts because I can't, and I discussed it already in the past with my two colleagues, it seems to be not at all relevant for the outcome of this case. So therefore, I think it's mandatory for all of us to try to streamline the case and to avoid additional extremely problematic battlefields in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that when the drafters of the rules drafted Rule 94, it was exactly Your Honours' concerns that they were balancing the rights of the accused and judicial economy. It's for that purpose that we have a rule that says we don't have to re-litigate the same issues in different cases. And also require the same witnesses to come back and testify over and over again. Of all the allegations in our indictment, we've only asked the Court to take judicial notice of this one particular allegation for which, since Your Honour asked, we were unable to obtain witnesses who were willing to come back to The Hague and testify again. I don't think it's unfair to the accused if the Court finds this issue was litigated. My understanding - and to be honest, Ms. Sutherland is much more familiar with the Tadic case than I am - was that Mr. Tadic did contest some of the factual findings. It wasn't just an alibi defence. And the Court in that case had to find, beyond a reasonable doubt, that the killings took place and that they were connected to this joint criminal enterprise which is discussed in the paragraphs quoted in our motion. As far as Your Honours' suggestion that we drop allegation that is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. we are unable to prove, we completely agree with you. At the end of our case, if we are unable to present evidence in any way about an allegation we will drop it. But when the rules provide for means of proof which Rule 94 does, we suggest it's exactly this situation that Rule 94 was created for. We don't think it's against either the rights of the accused, nor is it -- nor does it violate the goal of judicial economy to ask the Court to take judicial notice; rather, it's precisely for judicial economy that we are asking that notice be taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the other hand, I think in this case, we saw that on the initiative of the accused himself or on the initiative of counsel, we came to an agreement on the admission under Rule 92 bis which really served the purposes of judicial economy. And I should like to know why for this special event we're expected to take judicial notice there is no testimony under 92 bis available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, all I can tell you is what I was told, is that the witnesses were not available. I would have to inquire further to know whether or not they were asked if they would be willing to present their evidence by way of Rule 92 bis, which requires them to indicate that they would be willing to come for cross-examination. I can check and see if we do have any notations about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I would invite the parties - we have time enough during the following days - to discuss this issue. And whether or not the parties can maybe agree to work under Rule 92 bis, and maybe cross-examination then be not necessary. But let us know as soon as possible, please, in writing in order that a decision can be prepared as soon as possible because the proceedings should not be delayed by these additional exercises. This brings me to another point: We are proceeding and coming close to the end of the Prosecution case. In order to allow the Defence to study in a responsible way to the incoming documents and motions, we hereby decide that no new document be presented later than Friday, 20th of September, 2002, by the end of the working day, save leave is granted by the Trial Chamber to do so because good cause is shown. The same is true for motions by both parties. May I then ask the parties whether or not they conferred already on the question, when would be the most appropriate point in time to have the pre-Defence conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I discussed it with my learned friend, and we agree that it would be the best if we have that Status Conference on the 8th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is agreed by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then the pre-Defence conference is hereby scheduled for the 8th of November. But nevertheless, the Chamber would appreciate if the other party and the Bench could be notified beforehand on the envisaged number of witnesses or special problems related to translation and so on in order to facilitate the proceedings and to assist the Defence where necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Your Honour, we would be requesting, although we agree to the 8th of November, that we receive some notice before that - I can discuss it with counsel - of the first witnesses for the Defence so we can begin to prepare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't want to work with deadlines already now. I think the message is clear, and we are aware of the problems the Defence has in this case with the preparation and summoning of witnesses and bringing them to The Hague. But as mentioned, let us know about all the problems as soon as possible. As we have seen during the last days, there will be always a way of assistance, and I am grateful to know that both parties have all the assistance by the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In this case, the Government of the entity of Republika Srpska acting through the Government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. May I then ask, what about documents? Yesterday I learned that some best originals were available, but unfortunately it was not possible for the Judges to see these documents. Could they please be presented. I take it that the Defence has seen the documents. Thank you. Do you want to make any observations on these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not at this moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask in the meantime, Madam Registrar, to check whether or not Document S308 or 18 was not yet admitted into evidence. It was Exhibit Number S308 where the Defence reserved the right to object because the best possible original was not available. It is now available. May I please hear your comments on this document. May the usher please show this document once more to the Defence, 308.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we object on the basis of authenticity. There is no visible signature of anybody on that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. For reasons given on similar occasions in the past, this document is now admitted into evidence as S308. But it should -- it remains open to source this document, S308. Has this led to any result already?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: These were documents seized in October of 2000 at the Prijedor health centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we then come to the Prosecution's submission of statement of expert witness pursuant to Rule 94 bis. Characteristics of a corpus of documents associated with the name of Milomir Stakic prepared by Andrew R. Corin. First, in order not to make a mistake, may I ask Madam Registrar to tell me whether this document has already been admitted into evidence for the purposes that we know on the transcript what we are discussing. It has not been admitted? What would be, then, the next following exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It has been admitted, Your Honour, as S1 -- S295.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: S295. And then the problem of my -- the issue of my concern, the attachment to this report as follows would be S295-1. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again, we have the problem before us that we have numerous documents where we have an exhibit number. We have numerous documents where we have 65 ter numbers. utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we didn't bring our copy with us today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May the usher please provide the Prosecutor with my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll have to actually confer with Mr. Corin. I believe that most of the ones that Your Honour is referring to are -- Mr. Corin has simply cited the Official Gazette number for those. So he went through the Gazette and cited those numbers, and those Gazettes themselves are in evidence. He simply cited the decision number in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So no doubt, it would be of assistance for us if we would have in the -- an updated table or attachment including the exhibit numbers of these Official Gazettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Actually, we're looking for someone right now to help complete part of the review of the other spreadsheet, and we're having trouble finding enough people to do that. utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. But then we can see where it stems from, and immediately, yes, try to find out whether we can follow the inferences drawn by Mr. Corin or not. Please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My learned friend was actually looking only at the table, but there are also numbers incorporated inside the text of the report which are also sometimes ERN numbers or 65 ter numbers. So if possible, to have all those numbers numbered according to S numbers; and another issue regarding the same document is that we are still waiting for the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt, it was already mentioned that the B/C/S -- the translation into B/C/S has priority, and then as soon as possible, please, the French translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another, if possible, to have those S numbers incorporated into a B/C/S translation as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I know this is difficult, but I tried myself in part to understand this, and it would be extremely helpful that the -- also the accused, with the limited facilities in the Detention Unit, has access to the content of this document that this be provided.
